passages.title: A structure does not determine every material property
passages.text: In plain weave, the weft alternates over and under individual warp threads. The appearance of a textile also depends on the material and the properties of its threads.
passages.context: Original paraphrase of the technical description. It supports the generic interlacing idea, not this paper procedure, a unique cultural origin or a claim to represent all Greek textile practice.

claims.text: The specified checkerboard plan alternates at adjacent crossings in both directions.
claims.qualification: An ideal binary model with equally spaced strips; not a measurement of a real specimen.

claims.text: Correct symbolic alternation does not establish physical handling skill or fabric properties.
claims.qualification: Tension, packing, drape, continuous yarn and finished edges are outside this model.

context: In this diagram, warp strips W1–W6 form columns and weft strips F1–F6 form rows. These chosen axes are not a universal orientation for every woven object.
Front convention: the weft is above the warp when the row and column numbers sum to an even number. The bit string stores that front relation only.
Back view means turning the specimen over about a vertical axis: top stays top, warp labels reverse order, and the visible top strip at every crossing changes. It is not a rotation within the plane.
A six-column checkerboard may look the same after reversing columns and swapping visible strips. Trace the labels to establish that the view changed.

The error control changes a symbolic crossing only. It can produce a run of three repeated crossings in an interior row. The repair control models withdrawing and reweaving the whole selected weft strip.
A real repair requires accessible, unsealed ends and support for neighboring strips. Those strips may move; physical feasibility and instruction clarity have not been observed.

steps.text: Plan F1 across W1–W6 as over, under, over, under, over, under when viewed from the front. The diagram is a schematic, not a photograph.

steps.title: 2 · Reverse the phase
steps.text: Plan F2 as under, over, under, over, under, over. Adjacent rows now alternate at the same warp crossing.

steps.title: 3 · Continue the first phase

steps.title: 4 · Continue the second phase

steps.title: 6 · Inspect both sides and plan a repair
steps.text: Plan F6 like F2. For a real demonstration, photograph the labelled front, turn about the vertical axis and photograph the back. A proposed repair withdraws the entire chosen weft, supports its neighbors and reweaves the required sequence. This still needs physical verification.

# P07 independent AI artifact desk review

Date: 2026-10-22.
Reviewer: `atlas-ai-history-review`, independent AI source/context and conceptual-model reviewer. I do not claim textile-practitioner, conservator, lawyer or accessibility-observer credentials. This report supplements `/tmp/atlas-p07-source-review.md`; it is not physical pilot acceptance.

## Exact candidate and verification

Worktree: `/Users/teodev/.codex/worktrees/universal-pilots-integration/theorems-visualizations`.
Candidate: `x-craft-0001`, revision `0.1.0`, `draft` / `local-preview`.

I read `explorations/craft.json`, `practice-model.mjs`, the craft branches of `studio-views.mjs` and `studio-ui.mjs`, shared dispatch/acceptance checks, `docs/pilots/research/craft-physical-session.md`, `studio-original-assets.md` and the supplied craft HTML. No browser, repository edit, new source retrieval, nested reviewer or other-chat message was used. The prior successful ARTEX body read remains the source-check basis; no fresh verification is implied.

Using a separately written canonical serializer and Node crypto, I recomputed SHA-256 from current content and all thirteen builder-listed code files plus actual related collection labels. Results match `/tmp/atlas-studio-digests.json`:

- Content digest: `9ea0f5a3b1dd5aba4f27b1b69d533c6a6941b43fa6cd236ac65d1044cd867dac`.
- Artifact digest: `d0cb08ce1ff1c1226a3806ec278c068a6c4681dff6e87d2f5f40255d5869428e`.

Rendering the current candidate in memory with actual registry labels exactly matches `/tmp/atlas-studio-review-pages/x-craft-0001.html`. This is static/code inspection, not browser usability evidence or a claim that all repository checks passed.

## Findings

**No required repair found within this bounded conceptual desk review.** The implementation incorporates the source/design review's principal cautions:

- The source passage is marked editorial paraphrase, with a stable source/locator, selected-text hash and an explicit boundary between generic interlacing and a demonstrated paper procedure/cultural representation.
- Canonical warp columns W1–W6 and weft rows F1–F6 are disclosed, with a front/top convention. Front-relative data is separate from which strip is visible on the chosen side.
- Back view reverses canonical warp-label display and complements visible weft/warp at the same canonical crossing. It does not mutate canonical bits. The page warns that the six-column checkerboard can look the same after this operation.
- Error toggling is described as a symbolic plan change; text acknowledges a possible run of three interior repeated crossings. The diagnosis explicitly counts adjacent repeated pairs and separately reports departures from the specified starting phase. It does not mislabel the equally alternating opposite phase as necessarily invalid plain weave.
- Repair restores all six crossings of the selected canonical weft row to the declared front phase. The log is explicitly a record of symbolic operations, not physical making. Accessible unsealed ends, neighboring-strip support and possible movement remain disclosed.

I independently checked all 36 baseline crossings against the stated one-based even-sum phase; checked back-view complement and `7-column` display mapping; and toggled/repaired each possible single crossing. Each toggle produced exactly one baseline mismatch, and each whole-strip repair restored the baseline in that single-error scenario. This does not prove physical extraction, stability, motor skill or every possible runtime interaction. The integration owner is separately testing UI behavior.

The construction-stage UI distinguishes planned front relation from whether a weft has yet been inserted; edit/repair controls are disabled for a selected uninserted row. Diagram and table distinguish empty stages from crossings. The front/back/repair wording is consistent with the proposed physical-session packet.

## Reuse and asset honesty

The authored paraphrase remains consistent with the previously inspected [ARTEX technical description](https://artextiles.org/en/node/185). No source photograph is embedded in the reviewed code/content. The displayed diagrams are generated original schematics and are explicitly identified as such. The source/reuse decision does not infer general image licensing or endorsement from access.

The original-assets document records a proposed CC BY 4.0 release for applicable original material as a pending owner decision, rather than an existing repository-wide licence or an asserted signature. Future actual photographs require their own creator/participant permissions and terms. This supports a scoped local-draft reuse assessment, not legal or public-distribution clearance.

## Physical evidence and acceptance boundary

The draft repeatedly states that the real specimen, photographs, practitioner check, second-person reproduction and observed sessions do not exist. The physical-session packet contains an actual capture checklist, materials to verify, canonical front/back labels, a specified F3/W2 error, whole F3 extraction/reweaving, independent reproduction and blank receipt fields. It does not prefill a pass or present generated images as specimen evidence.

The record retains learning/accessibility review requirements with no passing receipts. Independently, the contract explicitly rejects acceptance of a `weave-structure` record because the physical-evidence/asset acceptance contract is not yet implemented. This is appropriate for the stated draft. Adding conceptual content/provenance/rights receipts must not be used to bypass that rejection or the missing physical evidence.

## Scoped dimension decisions for these hashes

| Dimension | AI desk-review decision and limits |
| --- | --- |
| content | passed — conceptual interlacing model, coordinate/front-back conventions, symbolic whole-strip repair and reader-facing limitation statements |
| provenance | passed — named institutional source and original schematic distinction, without a fabricated specimen or physical observation |
| rights | passed — documented reference/original explanation and local schematic-draft scope; source images excluded; proposed public terms remain pending; no legal/public-release clearance |
| learning | not reviewed/passed — no learner or physical reproduction session |
| accessibility | not reviewed/passed — no actual screen-reader or task observation |
| physical/practitioner competence | not established — no specimen, photographs, practitioner validation or second-person reproduction |

These three bounded AI passes can be retained as scoped desk-review evidence for this exact draft. The full craft pilot remains unaccepted. Any later code/content change requires the corresponding exact-artifact recheck; actual physical evidence requires the real session and a reviewed asset/observation contract.

# P07 real-sample and reproduction packet

Status: prepared, **no physical session performed**. Applies to `x-craft-0001` revision 0.1.0 and the corresponding schematic model. It does not establish that the proposed paper setup or repair works. The independent [source/design review](craft-source-review.md) explains the evidence limits.

## Proposed specimen to review before making

Use twelve pre-cut paper strips, six warp and six weft, with a flat support and removable edge support. A starting proposal is strips about 2 cm wide and 20 cm long, leaving accessible ends around the six-by-six crossing area. These dimensions and paper stiffness are not physically tested; the practitioner must record or revise them before freezing the session instructions.

Use large, high-contrast sets distinguished by written W/F labels as well as color/pattern. Put W1–W6 and F1–F6 labels on both sides near the ends so canonical identities remain readable after a flip. Add a top marker and a distinct front marker. Record actual strip dimensions, thickness/type, spacing, lighting, edge support and any assistance. Keep the weft ends unsealed; any temporary support must be described and removable for the demonstrated extraction. Do not infer stability from the schematic.

The declared front sequence for F1 is over/under/over/under/over/under across W1–W6. F2 has the opposite phase; subsequent rows alternate these phases. Back view turns about a vertical axis: top stays top, W6 becomes the leftmost visible warp label, and which strip is exposed at a crossing reverses. An in-plane rotation is not this back view.

## Required actual observations and assets

| Evidence ID | Capture or observation | Required record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| materials | Actual labelled strips and support | Dimensions/materials, creator/date, setup and assistance |
| step-0 | Warp layout and orientation markers | W1–W6 identity and accessible ends |
| step-1 | Actual first weft inserted | Front-relative sequence and any difficulty |
| step-2 | Opposite-phase second weft | Row and column alternation |
| front-complete | Actual completed specimen | All canonical IDs and front/top markers |
| back-complete | Same specimen after declared turn | Reversed warp-label order, same canonical crossings |
| error | Deliberately wrong F3/W2 relation | Actual over/under run; this interior change can create three consecutive weft-over crossings |
| extraction | Whole F3 withdrawn, neighbors supported | What moved, buckled or required assistance |
| reweaving | Whole F3 reinserted in the required phase | Intermediate steps and physical feasibility |
| repaired-front/back | Repaired specimen on both sides | Comparison to canonical table; remaining defects |

These entries are requirements, not existing images. Keep original files, creator, date, specimen/instruction revision, captions and explicit contributor/asset permission. Generated illustrations cannot fill a photograph slot. Caption only what the actual frame establishes. Record failed attempts and resulting instruction revisions rather than replacing them with the intended result.

## Independent reproduction

After a practitioner checks the actual demonstrated instructions, a second person attempts the frozen task using the supplied materials and instructions. Obtain consent and use a nonidentifying participant code; no contact or recruitment is authorized by this packet alone. Record the route (independent/partner-assisted/digital conceptual), assistance actually given, misunderstood steps, structural errors, front/back explanation and attempted repair. A demonstrator must not silently correct the second specimen.

Evaluate three outcomes separately: structural plan consistency, physical sequence completion, and observed handling. Digital clicking can support only the structural task. Do not grade inferred dexterity, tension control, drape or knowledge of an entire textile tradition. Ask the participant to transfer the label/flip reasoning to a new four-by-four diagram and explain what the diagram cannot establish.

## Blank receipt fields

- Exact instruction/model revision and artifact hash:
- Practitioner identity/role and scope actually checked:
- Specimen/material/support description:
- Asset paths, hashes, creator, permission and captions:
- Reproduction participant code and consent record reference:
- Route and assistance:
- Observed successes, failures and limits:
- Changes required and subsequent recheck:
- Review date and decision:

No field is prefilled as a pass. After genuine evidence arrives, implement and review the physical-evidence/asset contract before accepting the full P07 pilot. The present validator deliberately rejects that acceptance claim.
